title: Australia brings a second cash distribution company within its new regulatory framework
summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia designated Prosegur Australia Pty Ltd under the Cash Distribution Framework Act 2026. Prosegur Australia is a wholly owned subsidiary of Linfox Armaguard Pty Limited, which had itself been designated on September 3. The RBA’s November 6 announcement therefore matters even though ownership did not change. Parent and subsidiary are separate legal entities. A legislative instrument naming the subsidiary brings that entity within the framework established to support the continuity, resilience and efficiency of physical cash distribution.

The instrument identifies the subsidiary by its corporate number, 004 247 358. Governor Michele Bullock signed it on November 5. The commencement provision says it takes effect on the day after registration. The explanatory statement distinguishes that immediate change in legal status from what might happen later. Obligations applying to designated businesses come from the Act. Certain powers, including crisis resolution actions, become available only when the relevant statutory conditions are satisfied. The act of naming an entity does not itself exercise those powers.

That sequence affects how customers, lenders and investors should interpret the notice. Extending the regulatory perimeter can change which company the authorities can act upon if cash distribution is threatened. It does not establish that the operator already faces a disruption, that public funding has been supplied or that any customer has suffered a loss. The documents give no operating cost, route volumes, profitability figures or change to commercial prices. An estimate of the financial effect requires identifying which obligations now apply to the subsidiary and the activities it actually carries out.

The explanatory statement says merits review is unavailable for the designation under subsection 190(1). Parliamentary disallowance and periodic review nevertheless remain available. This distinction locates the channels for scrutinising a decision about the company’s status. It does not establish how any later action taken under a different statutory power would be reviewed.

The RBA consulted the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission as the Act requires, and also consulted Prosegur Australia. The explanatory statement records why it judged additional public consultation unnecessary. A single entity was directly affected by the designation, and the underlying law had already gone through public consultation and parliamentary committee scrutiny. The instrument itself remains subject to parliamentary scrutiny, including disallowance and sunsetting. The statement also discusses the confidentiality provisions in the broader framework and the risk that disclosure in a crisis could jeopardise continuity. It records no secrecy determination specific to this company.

For a business that depends on timely cash deliveries, the important question is where the legal contracts, staff, vehicles and operational dependencies sit within the group. Parent-level oversight and subsidiary-level oversight can have different implications if an interruption occurs at the company actually holding a critical contract. A more complete legal perimeter cannot by itself show how much spare capacity exists, how easily another operator could substitute or what a bank or retailer would have to pay for service. The RBA announcement and the two federal legislative documents establish the perimeter change. They leave its operational and financial consequences to be assessed against evidence of delivery capacity and obligations.

questions.question: Which services and obligations now sit inside the regulated subsidiary?
questions.detail: Map customer contracts, operating assets, staff and intercompany arrangements separately at Prosegur Australia and its already designated parent. Identify where the company signing a contract differs from the one actually transporting cash. This determines the direct reach of the designation and the residual dependencies.

questions.question: What would show a measurable improvement in cash access?
questions.detail: Compare route coverage, service disruptions, recovery times and feasible alternative providers across locations. Stress an interruption affecting just the subsidiary and one affecting the entire group. Naming a second entity may improve oversight even where the physical resources to substitute for an interrupted provider remain scarce.

questions.question: How much of a financial effect is attributable to the instrument?
questions.detail: Separate the obligations activated by designated status from contingent resolution measures requiring additional conditions. Look for actual compliance spending, contract amendments or recognised liabilities before estimating the effect on earnings or credit. Distinguish obligations borne within the subsidiary from guarantees or commitments carried at its parent.

questions.question: Which facts would signal an actual intervention in future?
questions.detail: Look for a subsequent instrument, direction or action taken under the relevant power and identify the entity affected. A fresh action with specific conditions would have different consequences for counterparties from continuation of ordinary supervision.

limitation: The release, designation and explanatory statement identify a regulated entity but supply no operating-volume estimate, pricing change or finding of distress.
